transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-03-04
Start time: 15:32 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Morales (Redwood SE), Maya Patel (Lumina CTO), Ravi Singh (Head of ML), Elena Gomez (Infra), Samir Khan (Security), Olivia Park (PM)

Summary: Quick discovery to understand Lumina's integration needs for deploying LLM features across patient-facing products. Key topics: SDK support, LangChain/LlamaIndex compatibility, gateway/proxy patterns, rate limits/quotas, observability hooks, and hosted vs dedicated vs private trade-offs. Agreed next steps: send security pack, share integration examples, provision trial creds, schedule POC baseline.

Topics: integration-architecture, SDKs, LangChain, LlamaIndex, proxy/gateway, rate-limits, observability, SOC2/KMS, VPC/private deploys

[00:00] Avery Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um this is Avery from Redwood, i'm the AE on the account, with me is Diego, our solutions engineer. quick roundtable?
[00:08] Maya Patel: hi, i'm maya, cto at lumina, we run the clinical decision support and patient messaging stacks.
[00:12] Ravi Singh: ravi, head of ml, mostly responsible for model infra and integrations.
[00:16] Elena Gomez: elena infra, i handle kubernetes, vpc peering and network security.
[00:20] Samir Khan: samir, security, i'll be looking at compliance, kms, audit logs.
[00:24] Avery Chen: great, thanks. goal today: figure out how you'd plug Redwood into your stack, whether hosted, dedicated, or private makes sense, and what the engineering work looks like.

[01:05] Diego Morales: quick agenda — ask a few questions about current stack and traffic, walk through SDKs + LangChain examples, discuss gateway/proxy and rate limit patterns, and then talk observability hooks and security.

[02:10] Ravi Singh: high level, we have a mix of low-latency patient queries (chat-like), and higher-throughput batch summarization of notes overnight. latency matters for the chat flows, p95 target is ~300ms for single-turn generation, but we can tolerate a bit more for multi-turn. cost is also important; we process millions of tokens monthly.

[03:05] Avery Chen: ok good, so two distinct profiles — latency-critical interactive and batch. are you currently using any hosted LLM providers?
[03:14] Ravi Singh: yes, we're on a mix — some endpoints on commodity cloud GPUs and some calls to openai, and a few self-hosted models for inference. but managing variance in latency and cost is a headache.

[04:00] Maya Patel: security is a big question. patient data, HIPAA-ish constraints, we need audit logs, encrypted at rest/in transit, and ideally a private deployment option.

[04:28] Diego Morales: understood. Redwood supports hosted API for quick start, Dedicated reserved pools for predictable throughput, and Private (VPC/on-prem) for strict compliance. on hosted we offer SOC2 controls and encryption, but for full network isolation you'd look at Dedicated with VPC or Private with a customer-controlled plane.

[05:02] Elena Gomez: on the Private option, do you provide an OVA or helm chart? how much ops work on our side?
[05:12] Diego Morales: for private we have a deployable package — there's a customer-managed control plane that can run in their VPC or on-prem. typical deployment is helm charts + operator, we provide manifests, but you'll need to run the infra (k8s, nodes, etc). for Dedicated we provision the GPU pools and you get a private tenancy with peering options.

[06:00] Ravi Singh: what about SDKs — we primarily use Python, and a lot of our orchestration is via LangChain and LlamaIndex. how first-class is that?

[06:14] Diego Morales: good question. our Python SDK has dedicated helpers for LangChain and LlamaIndex, we also have REST/HTTP and node SDKs. we maintain example repos showing LangChain chains, retrievers wired to LlamaIndex, and vector store adapters. i'll send the sample repo after this call.

[06:45] Olivia Park: do you provide out-of-the-box retriever/embedding connectors? we use a hosted vector DB (managed pinecone-like).

[06:53] Diego Morales: yes, Redwood has embedding endpoints and common vector store adapters; we include examples for Pinecone, Milvus, and Weaviate. embeddings are billed separately and you can pin models for embeddings vs generation.

[07:30] Maya Patel: integration pattern question — do you recommend calling Redwood directly from our backend, or use an internal gateway/proxy?

[07:38] Avery Chen: many enterprise customers use an internal gateway pattern for auth, request validation, rate limiting, and routing. Redwood can be called directly or behind your gateway — we provide JWT/SAML service credentials and network peering options. for hosted customers, the gateway handles auth and mapping to API keys. for private/dedicated, you can terminate within your VPC.

[08:20] Elena Gomez: if we put a proxy in front, we need to preserve streaming responses for chat. do you support gRPC or streaming websockets through proxy?

[08:30] Diego Morales: streaming is supported over HTTP/1.1 chunked and WebSocket. gRPC is in our roadmap but currently we recommend proxy passthrough for chunked streaming. proxied websockets are common; we have docs on Nginx and envoy configs. small note: some proxies buffer by default — you'll need to disable buffering to preserve low latency streaming.

[09:10] Samir Khan: audit logs — is there token-level trace, who called what, and redaction controls?

[09:18] Diego Morales: yes, audit logs with request metadata, model version, tokens counts, and timestamps. in hosted we retain logs per plan; for private/dedicated we can stream logs to your SIEM via secure syslog or S3. PII redaction is a feature we offer — we can redact or avoid storing request bodies on ingest depending on contract.

[10:05] Ravi Singh: rate limits and quotas — our usage spikes at certain times, and we'd like soft quotas and graceful degradation. how does Redwood handle throttling?

[10:18] Avery Chen: Redwood offers per-API-key quotas and per-customer rate limits. you can configure soft and hard limits, plus fallback policies that route to a smaller/cheaper model or cached responses. for Dedicated we can reserve capacity and set bursting policies. we also have token-level cost reporting to help tune policies.

[11:12] Olivia Park: do you support request-level priority? e.g., urgent clinical alerts should preempt analytics jobs.

[11:20] Diego Morales: yes our smart routing supports priority lanes; you can tag requests with priority and route to reserved pools or higher-SLO instances. that's often used when mixing analytic batch loads and real-time user-facing traffic.

[12:00] Maya Patel: i'm worried about model drift and quality regressions — do you provide evals or regression alerts?

[12:08] Diego Morales: Redwood Optimize handles quality monitoring — you can push canonical prompt sets and we can run continuous evals and alert on regressions (precision/recall style metrics or custom heuristics). this ties into rollouts so you can canary a new model variant and monitor before full rollout.

[13:00] Ravi Singh: for the POC we'd like a baseline latency and cost comparison between our current self-host and Redwood hosted/dedicated. what telemetry do you need?

[13:12] Avery Chen: sample traffic profile (qps distribution, payload sizes, prompt lengths, typical max sequence length), a set of representative prompts, and target SLOs. Diego can run a benchmark against hosted and dedicated configs and produce p50/p95/p99 latencies and cost per token.

[14:00] Elena Gomez: network — for dedicated VPC peering what's the egress path? do calls go over public internet or direct peer?

[14:10] Diego Morales: Dedicated supports private network peering (VPC peering), so traffic stays on private links. hosted API still uses public endpoints unless you contract a dedicated private endpoint. Private deployment is fully customer controlled.

[15:00] Samir Khan: KMS integrations: do you support customer-managed keys for model artifacts and audit logs?

[15:08] Diego Morales: yes — for Private we support KMS/HSM integration. for Dedicated we offer BYOK for storage encryption and you can route logs to your encrypted bucket. Hosted supports envelope encryption with Redwood-managed keys, or enterprise customers can request BYOK under contract.

[16:20] Ravi Singh: in terms of SDK auth — do you use API keys only or support short-lived tokens from our identity provider?

[16:28] Avery Chen: both. API keys are typical for quickstarts, but we support federated auth (OIDC) and can issue short-lived tokens via SAML/OIDC flows for tighter control.

[17:05] Olivia Park: size of the footprint if we go private on-prem — do you have recommended minimum GPU/CPU specs?

[17:12] Diego Morales: yes, we have a hardware sizing guide. for smaller LLMs a single A10 or T4 node can work for dev; production private deployments typically use clusters with multiple A100/V100 equivalents depending on throughput and model size. we'll share the sizing doc.

[18:00] Maya Patel: what about model compatibility — we primarily run open weights tuned in-house and some Llama derivatives. will Redwood accept custom model binaries?

[18:10] Diego Morales: we onboard custom models via our model packaging process; we verify architecture compatibility and may recommend quantization profiles. for hosted we have curated models but also allow bringing your own model to Dedicated/Private. there can be some performance tuning needed.

[19:05] Ravi Singh: can you do dynamic model routing, like route to smaller cheaper model for low-priority calls?

[19:12] Avery Chen: yes that's part of smart routing — policy based routing by latency/cost/priority/region. you can set fallbacks to a quantized variant for cheaper inference.

[20:00] Elena Gomez: observability hooks — what telemetry do we get? traces, spans, per-token cost breakdown?

[20:08] Diego Morales: we export structured telemetry: request traces, token counts, model version, latency breakdown by stage (tokenization, kernel, kv miss/hit), and you can ingest into Datadog/Lightstep/NewRelic. we also expose per-route dashboards in Redwood Console.

[21:05] Samir Khan: retention policy — for audit/log retention and request bodies?

[21:12] Diego Morales: retention is configurable. hosted has tiered retention per plan; enterprise Dedicated/Private lets you control retention or export to your archives. we can also opt to not persist request bodies for privacy-sensitive workloads.

[22:00] Maya Patel: billing — token based or instance-based?

[22:06] Avery Chen: hosted is usage-based (per token + embeddings). Dedicated is typically reserved capacity + overage; Private is licensed + infra. for POC we can provide sample cost estimates given your traffic profile.

[23:10] Ravi Singh: any tricky gotchas when integrating with LangChain or LlamaIndex?

[23:18] Diego Morales: a few practical notes — LangChain chains often expect sync vs async semantics; our SDK supports both patterns. LlamaIndex retrievers often assume synchronous embed calls; batching embeddings is important for cost. also watch for streaming/delta vs non-streaming behavior when you wrap chains — some wrappers swallow events. we have examples and tests.

[24:30] Olivia Park: can we bring our own observability keys or integrations for traces?

[24:36] Diego Morales: yes you can configure exporters and we can push traces to your collector, or allow Redwood Console to correlate traces with console logs.

[25:00] Avery Chen: let's pivot to next steps — we'll send security pack and sample repos. Diego will run a small benchmark once we get your sample prompts and traffic profile. Elena, could you share who will own the infra sizing?

[25:12] Elena Gomez: i'll own it, i'll send the current cluster specs and baseline traffic by end of week.

[26:00] Maya Patel: timeline — we want to decide by end of Q2. POC ideally in two weeks.

[26:08] Avery Chen: sounds good. for the POC we can start with hosted trial to validate functionality, then spin up a Dedicated test pool for latency runs, and if needed scope Private.

[27:15] Ravi Singh: security team will want to review SOC2+ and network diagrams. Samir will take the owner on that.

[27:22] Samir Khan: yes i'll review, also want to run a short threat model around potential data exfil.

[28:10] Diego Morales: for the benchmark we typically measure 1000 requests across your p95 prompt length distribution, measure p50/p95/p99, and cost per 1k tokens. we'll send a template for sample prompts.

[29:05] Olivia Park: question — do you support model version pinning and rollbacks via the API?

[29:12] Diego Morales: yep, you can pin model versions per-route and perform canary rollouts via the console or API. automatic rollback triggers can be set on error/latency/quality thresholds.

[30:00] Maya Patel: curious about fallback policies for quota exhaustion — can you return a cached response or degrade to a shorter summary?

[30:12] Avery Chen: yes you can configure fallback actions: return cached reply, call a cheaper model, or degrade to a deterministic template. some customers implement a graceful fallback in their gateway to preserve UX.

[31:20] Ravi Singh: on the billing sample — can you give a rough cost comparison now?

[31:28] Avery Chen: rough rules of thumb: hosted managed larger models might be ~X per 1k tokens (we'll send precise numbers in the pricing doc); Dedicated reduces unit cost for sustained throughput; Private depends on your infra amortization. we'll provide an apples-to-apples comparison in the followup.

[32:30] Elena Gomez: curious about maintenance windows and upgrades for Private — how are kernel upgrades handled?

[32:38] Diego Morales: for Private you control the upgrade cadence; Redwood publishes upgrade bundles and we recommend canarying across nodes. for Dedicated we coordinate rolling upgrades with minimal disruption and provide scheduled maintenance windows.

[33:45] Maya Patel: we have a compliance requirement to have SSO via SAML and SCIM provisioning. do you support that?

[33:52] Avery Chen: yes SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning are supported for enterprise accounts; we'll include integration guides.

[34:20] Samir Khan: any third-party data processors? we need subprocessors list for our legal team.

[34:28] Avery Chen: we'll include our subprocessors and the data processing addendum in the security pack.

[35:10] Diego Morales: small note on quantization — if you bring large weights we often recommend quantizing to reduce memory and cost; we provide recommended quant profiles and have empirical perf data per model family.

[36:05] Ravi Singh: do you support per-tenant billing or per-route cost allocation?

[36:12] Avery Chen: Redwood Console supports cost breakdowns by API key, route, and model; you can map to tenant metadata for chargeback.

[37:20] Olivia Park: if we need ephemeral tokens for mobile clients, is there a recommended pattern?

[37:28] Diego Morales: yes — issue short-lived tokens from your backend after auth, then call Redwood from mobile with ephemeral creds. avoid embedding long-lived API keys in clients.

[38:10] Maya Patel: are there any hard limits on model sizes we can host with Dedicated?

[38:18] Diego Morales: no hard limits — depends on hardware and kernel support; very large models may need sharding across nodes. we'll collaborate on sizing for large models.

[39:05] Ravi Singh: integration timeline — from POC to production, what does a typical customer take?

[39:12] Avery Chen: something like 4-8 weeks for simple integrations (hosted + SDK), 8-12 weeks for Dedicated, and 3-6 months for full Private on-prem depending on compliance and infra constraints.

[40:10] Elena Gomez: for the POC can we limit data retention and have logs delivered to our S3?

[40:18] Diego Morales: yes, logs can be exported and we can configure retention to zero for request bodies.

[41:05] Olivia Park: any recommended change to our current architecture?

[41:12] Diego Morales: minimal — introduce a gateway layer for auth and priority tagging, batch embeddings in background jobs, and route interactive traffic to a reserved pool or dedicated lane.

[42:00] Maya Patel: ok let's recap next steps.

[42:05] Avery Chen: recap — Avery to send security pack + subprocessors + pricing doc; Diego to share SDK quickstart, LangChain/LlamaIndex repo, and benchmark template; Elena to send infra specs and traffic profile; Lumina to review SOC2 and schedule POC week of Mar 14.

[42:40] Ravi Singh: yep i'll assemble the prompt set and target SLOs and share with Diego.

[43:10] Samir Khan: i'll review security docs and follow up with any ATO questions.

[44:00] Avery Chen: great — i'll follow up with calendar invites and the trial keys. last question, anything else we missed?

[44:08] Maya Patel: maybe just one more: does Redwood support model editing or fine-tuning pipelines?

[44:16] Diego Morales: we don't host full training pipelines in hosted; we support fine-tuning/adapter workflows for some models and can integrate with your training infra for Private deployments.

[45:00] Olivia Park: thanks everyone — that was helpful.

[45:05] Avery Chen: thanks all, talk soon.

[51:28] Call ended
